successCriteria: the target Java version is resolved or explicitly assumed

scenarios.title: Review or generate loss-safe Paper item delivery
scenarios.userPrompt: Give a player a reward without losing or duplicating items when the inventory is full.
useWhen: the request inserts rewards, refunds, restored items, or other stacks into a player inventory
the request mentions a full inventory, partial insertion, uninserted leftovers, or an overflow drop
the implementation retries or persists an item delivery after insertion or fallback failure
successCriteria: the target Paper version and every selected insertion or fallback member are verified
every requested stack reaches an inserted, recovered fallback, deferred or rejected, or preserved-for-caller failure outcome exactly once
the implementation reports completion only after all uninserted stacks follow the selected overflow policy
complete, partial, full-inventory, and retry paths plus selected fallback failure when applicable are covered by tests
mustAvoid: ignoring uninserted stacks returned by a partial inventory insertion
sending the original requested stack to a fallback after part of it may already be inserted
assuming Player.give exists or has the same overflow behavior on every Paper version
dropping overflow without an explicit recipient pickup or ownership and notification policy
scenarios.failureMode: A reward path can silently destroy overflow items or duplicate the portion already inserted when fallback and retry handling are incomplete.

scenarios.title: Review or generate safe Paper custom inventory GUI interactions
scenarios.userPrompt: Create or review a custom Paper inventory GUI that protects its items from clicks, drags, swaps, transfers, collection, and stale close or reopen behavior.
useWhen: the request creates a custom inventory GUI, chest menu, selector, shop, or other virtual inventory view
the request handles InventoryClickEvent or InventoryDragEvent
the request mentions shift-click, hotbar or number-key swap, offhand swap, double-click, collect-to-cursor, drag, top inventory, bottom inventory, allowed slots, cancellation, close, or reopen
the request asks whether GUI items can be moved, duplicated, deleted, collected, or stolen through alternate inventory gestures
successCriteria: the owned view is identified independently of mutable title text and both click and drag events are cancelled before policy branches
top, bottom, and outside clicks are classified while shift transfer, hotbar and offhand swap, and double-click collection remain denied unless explicitly modeled
an allowed drag requires every raw slot in its footprint to be allowed
GUI buttons stay cancelled while their actions are applied manually and deprecated InventoryClickEvent.setCursor is never used
every editable top slot has per-session or deliberately shared ownership plus one atomic settlement transition with an explicit full-inventory overflow outcome
commit, close, replacement view, disconnect, death, shutdown, and repeated callbacks settle each owned stack exactly once
close, open, and reopen work from click, drag, and InventoryCloseEvent handlers is deferred and guarded against stale players, views, GUI sessions, or settled state
mustAvoid: cancelling only when clickedInventory equals the top inventory
handling InventoryClickEvent while omitting InventoryDragEvent
allowing bottom inventory clicks without separately denying actions that target or scan the top inventory
accepting a drag because at least one affected raw slot is allowed
uncancelling a GUI button click before manually applying its action
using deprecated InventoryClickEvent.setCursor for manual cursor changes
allowing editable top slots without an ownership, terminal settlement, and overflow policy
returning, persisting, dropping, or consuming the same editable stack from more than one lifecycle callback or queued task
closing, opening, or reopening a view directly inside an InventoryClickEvent, InventoryDragEvent, or InventoryCloseEvent callback
scenarios.failureMode: A custom GUI can leak or corrupt items when alternate click, drag, cursor collection, cross-inventory transfer, deprecated cursor mutation, editable-slot ownership, settlement, overflow, or lifecycle paths are not part of the allowlist.

scenarios.title: Review or generate an operable Paper administrative command
scenarios.userPrompt: Create or review a Paper administrative command that operators can authorize, invoke from the right sender contexts, inspect, reload, and recover safely.
useWhen: the request creates or reviews an administrator, moderator, operator, maintenance, or configuration command
the command changes persistent or runtime state and needs list, show, status, reload, retry, repair, reset, grant, revoke, or remove operations
the implementation assumes the sender is the target, is player-only without player-local input, or cannot be run from the server console
the request needs permission checks, explicit target selection, offline-player handling, failure feedback, bulk-operation confirmation, or reload recovery
successCriteria: the operational surface explicitly covers required mutation, inspection, reload, recovery, and retry paths, or documents why a path is intentionally unavailable

target-version player, local console, remote console, command block, command minecart, proxied, and custom sender kinds are explicitly supported or rejected from actual input and trust requirements, unknown subtype fallthrough is rejected, and privileged actions on another subject use an explicit target
online-only and offline-capable targets match whether live Bukkit state is truly required, and offline lookup distinguishes a stable known identity from unknown input
every privileged branch has an explicit permission policy and bulk or destructive scope requires deliberate confirmation or preview
reload validates a complete candidate before atomically replacing the effective state, preserves the last valid state on failure, and does not block the main server thread with I/O
typed outcomes report success, no target, invalid input or state, permission denial, partial completion, and I/O failure to the invoker
list, show, or status exposes the effective post-change state, and target notification is separate from invoker feedback
tests cover every supported and rejected sender kind, self, other target, online, offline, missing target, denied permission, reload failure, retry, bulk confirmation, and secret redaction
mustAvoid: making a command player-only when it needs no location, view, cursor, held item, or other player-local input
silently accepting or rejecting remote console, command block, command minecart, proxied, or custom CommandSender kinds, or letting an unknown subtype fall through
using the administrative sender as an implicit target for an operation that should name its subject
requiring an online Player for a database-only or configuration-only operation
treating an OfflinePlayer value as proof that an unknown target is registered or has joined
shipping a state-changing command without inspection, recovery, permission, or failure-result paths
replacing the active configuration before the entire reload candidate is valid
treating tab-completion filtering or command visibility as authorization
performing all-player or destructive mutations through an ambiguous default scope
notifying only the affected player while leaving a different invoker or the console without a result
accepting raw secrets as command arguments or exposing them through suggestions, histories, logs, results, status output, or audit records
scenarios.failureMode: A feature can exist in code yet remain unsafe or impossible to operate when its command surface omits console access, explicit targets, permissions, inspection, atomic reload, recovery, or observable outcomes.

scenarios.title: Review stable player identity and intentional display output
scenarios.userPrompt: Create or review Paper code that resolves, stores, synchronizes, and displays players without confusing stable identity, account names, and presentation labels.
useWhen: the request stores a player by UUID, account name, Player, OfflinePlayer, or profile
a command accepts a player name or must support a known offline player
messages, inventories, dialogs, tab lists, scoreboards, titles, notifications, logs, or external output display a player
renames, reconnects, cache invalidation, or cross-server propagation affect player data
successCriteria: stable player identity is distinct from mutable lookup input, current account name, optional display label, and rendered output

persistence and ownership use an identity authoritative for the documented online or trusted proxy mode and survive account-name changes only when authenticated identity or an independent account link supports it; direct offline mode otherwise states the limitation and never auto-remaps ownership, while unknown input cannot create or impersonate a known identity
online, known offline, unknown, invalid, ambiguous when applicable, and unavailable lookup outcomes are explicit

every human-facing surface names its intended label source, rich-text form, trust and markup policy, transport encoding and escaping, mention and control-character handling, Component event policy, null fallback, and disambiguation policy
external or remote lookup is bounded and off the main thread, with an explicit cache and refresh policy
cross-server updates converge under the declared authoritative sources and ordering rule
tests cover rename, offline and unknown state, duplicate labels, stale caches, lookup failure, reconnect, and each output transport
mustAvoid: using an account name, nickname, display component, or unauthenticated forwarded identifier as the only persistent player key
assuming UUID authority is unchanged across online-mode, offline-mode, or proxy-forwarding configuration changes
claiming rename continuity on direct offline mode without an independently authenticated account link, or automatically remapping ownership from a name
treating an OfflinePlayer instance as proof that the input identifies a known player
silently selecting Player.name, OfflinePlayer.name, displayName, or UUID for user-facing output
using a Component or decorated display label as a command lookup key

parsing an untrusted account name or display label as MiniMessage or other markup, allowing unintended external mentions or markup, retaining unsafe control characters, or forwarding unapproved Component click or hover events
blocking the main server thread on profile, database, or network resolution
letting stale server-local caches overwrite a newer account name or display label
testing only an online player whose account name never changes
scenarios.failureMode: Identity confusion can misattribute ownership and permissions, while implicit display choices expose raw identifiers or produce stale and inconsistent player labels.

scenarios.title: Review a Paper plugin message, custom payload, RPC, or chunked upload protocol
scenarios.userPrompt: Review this Paper plugin-message RPC codec and chunked upload flow for malformed payloads, spoofed player identity, request correlation, retries, timeouts, duplicate delivery, and lifecycle cleanup.
useWhen: the request creates or reviews Paper plugin messaging or a custom payload channel
the request implements RPC, a binary message codec, request correlation, or terminal responses
the request sends chunked uploads or retains request state across asynchronous work
successCriteria: channels are namespaced, registered, and unregistered with the plugin lifecycle using target-version verified API members

the versioned envelope has explicit message kinds and the decoder rejects malformed, trailing, unknown, oversized, over-nested, or over-decompressed data before allocation or before a bounded decompressor exceeds its output cap
authorization uses the authenticated connection or trusted proxy boundary rather than claimed payload identity
request IDs are session-scoped, duplicates are idempotent or rejected, and each accepted request receives at most one terminal response
timeouts, cancellation, reconnect, close, and disable clean request and upload state
an unavailable or closed player/connection carrier is handled explicitly rather than treating plugin messaging as durable standalone transport
concurrent requests and chunked uploads have ordering, checksum, total-size, expiry, queue, and backpressure bounds
retries are limited to declared idempotent operations, transport failures remain distinct from business outcomes, and Bukkit publication uses a safe execution context
hostile and exact-boundary tests exercise every decoder, allocation, lifecycle, duplicate, and concurrency rule
mustAvoid: hardcoding transport limits without target-version API constants or explicit evidence
treating Paper documentation examples as proof of a safe application codec
authorizing a player or proxy action from a UUID, name, permission, or role claimed inside the payload
allocating arrays, strings, collections, maps, nested objects, or decompressed buffers before validating their bounds, or decompressing without an enforced actual-output cap
letting request IDs, chunks, uploads, futures, or response state survive their connection/session or plugin lifecycle
retrying non-idempotent operations, merging transport errors into business outcomes, or issuing multiple terminal responses
performing blocking I/O or unsafe Bukkit state publication in a plugin-message callback
scenarios.failureMode: A plausible codec can still permit identity spoofing, memory or decompression denial of service, duplicate side effects, stale-session responses, unbounded uploads, or unsafe server-thread work.
